subject: Biotechnology
title: DNA Synthesis and Assembly
description: A quick win: understand DNA Synthesis and Assembly.

hook.text: Reading DNA is fast and cheap — writing it from scratch is where synthetic biology begins.

buildup.text: Chemical synthesis builds oligonucleotides letter by letter — then enzymatic assembly joins them into genes.

discovery.text: Gibson Assembly joins multiple DNA fragments in one reaction — overlapping ends guide seamless, scarless joining.

twist.text: Error rates limit length — synthesizing a whole genome requires error correction at every stage.

climax.text: DNA synthesis costs dropped from $10 per base in 2000 to under $0.05 today — Moore's Law for biology.

punchline.text: Type a sequence, receive DNA by mail — synthesis turns digital designs into biology.

quiz.question: What is Gibson Assembly?
options: A method to sequence DNA faster than conventional techniques
A one-step reaction that joins multiple DNA fragments using overlapping ends
A machine that prints proteins directly from DNA sequences

details.summary: DNA synthesis chemically builds custom DNA sequences from scratch, nucleotide by nucleotide. Assembly methods then join short synthesized fragments into longer constructs, enabling construction of entire genes, pathways, and even whole genomes that may not exist in nature.
details.whyItMatters: DNA synthesis frees synthetic biology from relying on existing natural sequences. The ability to write DNA de novo from a computer design is the manufacturing backbone of synthetic biology, analogous to semiconductor fabrication for electronics.
takeaways: Chemical synthesis builds DNA oligonucleotides up to about 200 bases long
Assembly methods like Gibson and Golden Gate join fragments into large constructs
Entire bacterial genomes have been assembled from synthesized DNA fragments

faq.question: How long of a DNA sequence can currently be synthesized?
faq.answer: Individual oligonucleotides are synthesized up to about 200 nucleotides. These are assembled into gene-length fragments of several thousand bases. Through hierarchical assembly, constructs exceeding a million base pairs have been built, including entire bacterial genomes.

faq.question: What assembly methods join short DNA fragments into longer sequences?
faq.answer: Gibson Assembly uses overlapping fragments joined by exonuclease, polymerase, and ligase in one reaction. Golden Gate uses Type IIS restriction enzymes for scarless ordered assembly. Both can join multiple fragments simultaneously into large multi-gene constructs.
